guidance_summary: September-quarter revenue is guided to grow 9%-11% year over year, including a roughly 2.5 percentage-point sequential FX headwind and materially greater supply-constraint impact. iPhone growth is expected in the mid-teens, while Services growth should be broadly similar to the June quarter before the 2.5-point FX effect. Gross margin is guided to 47%-48%, including an approximately 1-point tariff-refund benefit; operating expenses are expected at $19.1-$19.4 billion, other income and expense around $350 million excluding investment mark-to-market effects, and the tax rate around 16.5%. No capex guidance was provided.
key_qa_moments: Analysts pressed on the sharp September growth deceleration and whether supply constraints would worsen into December. Management attributed the issue primarily to unexpectedly strong iPhone and Mac demand, limited advanced-node flexibility, and acknowledged that Apple would be 'scrambling' on supply, while refusing to provide December guidance.

On memory inflation, Cook said Apple expects even higher costs in September and continuing price increases beyond that quarter. He described the situation as a '100-year flood,' said carry-in inventory benefits will diminish, and offered no clear sourcing or pricing solution beyond evaluating all options.

On Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, management expressed strong enthusiasm but admitted it is too early to determine compute economics or whether iCloud+ upgrades will offset costs, signaling meaningful uncertainty around AI monetization and capital intensity.

On Services, management provided unusually specific detail that FX was the primary growth headwind, but also disclosed mobile-gaming softness and U.S. App Store legal changes; September faces another 2.5-point sequential FX headwind.
risks: Advanced-node supply constraints are expected to affect iPhone, Mac, and iPad more severely in September, with no visibility beyond that quarter.
Memory prices are rising exponentially, pressuring product gross margins; management expects costs to increase further and inventory offsets to fade.
Foreign exchange is a disproportionate headwind to Services, amounting to roughly a 5-point impact to year-over-year growth from March through September.
AI infrastructure and compute costs could increase operating expense, cost of goods sold, and capital intensity, while monetization through iCloud+ remains unproven.
Services face mobile-gaming weakness, App Store business-model changes, and ongoing U.S. litigation exposure.
Siri AI rollout remains delayed or uncertain in the EU and China because of regulatory and approval requirements.
CEO succession introduces execution and strategic-transition risk as Tim Cook leaves the earnings-call role.
summary: Apple delivered a very strong June quarter, with 16% revenue growth, 22% iPhone growth, 29% Mac growth, and record cash flow, but results and gross margin benefited from tariff refunds. The forward outlook is materially less robust: September growth decelerates to 9%-11% amid worsening supply constraints, higher memory costs, and FX pressure, while Q&A revealed limited visibility into December, uncertain AI economics, and regulatory delays for Siri AI. Overall, the call is balanced between exceptional current demand and increasingly significant near-term execution and margin risks.

narrative: Investors should watch whether Apple’s Q4 results and guidance validate the optimism implied by its “earnings preview” coverage and the stock’s move toward an all-time high, particularly through iPhone demand, Services growth, and gross-margin commentary. The launch of Apple’s first touchscreen laptop could also prompt questions about product strategy, customer adoption, and whether it becomes a meaningful future growth driver, even though it is unlikely to materially affect this call. Given the broader “Magnificent 7” decline, management’s outlook and its explanation of how Apple is navigating valuation, competition, China exposure, and AI-related investment may matter as much as the reported quarter. My expectation is for solid execution and a constructive long-term message, but with elevated expectations making the market especially sensitive to weaker guidance or any sign that hardware demand is losing momentum.
